requirement:
`habeas coverage-check` MUST check saved execution coverage against
{cite}`requirements.test-coverage.check.threshold` and
{cite}`requirements.test-coverage.check.functions`, returning success only when
every applicable obligation is satisfied or has accepted exception evidence
under {cite}`requirements.test-coverage.check.exceptions`. The command MUST NOT
build the project, execute tests, collect coverage, or invoke an assessment model.
rationale:
The two tests marked for `requirements.test-coverage.check` are adequate for the subject's own obligations. I did not read the unit tests in `src/execution_coverage/check.rs`. My conclusion about them rests on their {test} references and the implementation snippets.

**Obligations derived from the subject**
1. `habeas coverage-check` checks saved coverage against `check.threshold` and `check.functions`. It succeeds only when every applicable obligation is satisfied or has accepted exception evidence.
2. It does not build, run tests, collect coverage or call an assessment model.

**Mapping to tests**
- **Success path.** `tests/execution_coverage.rs#fn[full_test_flow_checks_real_function_counters_after_all_tests]` runs the real full flow on a fixture and then runs the saved `coverage-check` (`saved_check`). It asserts success and "Coverage check passed".
- **Failure path, function obligation.** The same test rewrites the source so the nested `hidden` function has zero execution. It asserts that the exit status is a failure and that stdout reports `#fn[outer]/fn[hidden]: zero execution` and not an `outer` zero-execution line. The saved check then fails with "Coverage check failed". It also asserts that the recorded test run still reports success, so the policy caused the failure.
- **Failure path, unmeasured functions.** `fn[book_rendering_preserves_retained_coverage_and_never_launches_tests]` runs the standalone `habeas coverage-check` against a filtered, partial collection. It asserts a non-zero exit and that stdout contains the "File execution coverage" report.
- **No build, test run or collection.**
  - The standalone check runs with a `cargo` shim that records any non-`metadata` invocation and exits 99. The test asserts the forbidden-command file does not exist.
  - It also asserts that a sentinel file written by a test body is not recreated, so no test ran.
  - It asserts the retained coverage storage is byte-identical before and after.
  - The mdbook rendering path is checked in the same way.
- **No model call.** The full-flow test installs a `model_tripwire` server and asserts zero requests after both the full flow and the saved checks.
- **Evidence directory untouched.** `retained_files` on `evidence` is compared before and after.

**Obligations delegated elsewhere**
- Per-file threshold arithmetic, exact counts, unmeasured files and the no-executable-obligations case belong to `check.threshold`.
- Function attribution, including nested functions and closures, belongs to `check.functions`.
- Acceptance, staleness and non-transfer of exceptions belong to `check.exceptions`.
- Each of these has its own {test} items in `src/execution_coverage/check.rs`, such as `exact_per_file_threshold_and_partial_functions`, `accepted_file_and_function_explanations_remain_separate_from_execution` and `missing_and_stale_explanations_fail_the_report`. They assert on the report's `passed` flag, and the CLI maps that flag to the exit status.
- The CLI path is `main.rs#fn[main]`, which prints `report.text`. `check_saved` sets `passed = errors.is_empty()`, so every gap kind uses the same pass/fail path.
- The subject's tests need not repeat those cases. They do show that the command-level outcome flips between pass and fail. They also show that function-level and unmeasured gaps reach the exit status.

I found no plausible requirement-violating behaviour that these tests and the delegated tests would together accept. There is no applicable {fixme} acknowledgment.

text: :::{req} check
`habeas coverage-check` MUST check saved execution coverage against
{cite}`requirements.test-coverage.check.threshold` and
{cite}`requirements.test-coverage.check.functions`, returning success only when
every applicable obligation is satisfied or has accepted exception evidence
under {cite}`requirements.test-coverage.check.exceptions`. The command MUST NOT
build the project, execute tests, collect coverage, or invoke an assessment model.
:::{req} check.threshold
Each first-party Rust file under
{cite}`requirements.references.rust_item_coverage.parsing` MUST have at least 80%
execution coverage of its instrumented lines, or current accepted exception
evidence explaining why the file falls below that target under
{cite}`requirements.test-coverage.check.exceptions`. Counts MUST use the
file-and-line union rule of {cite}`requirements.test-coverage.index.summary`;
a line counts as executed when any eligible test process or its associated
child processes has a positive execution count for it.
The check MUST use the combined selection and freshness rules of
{cite}`requirements.test-coverage.index.selection` and
{cite}`requirements.test-coverage.index.freshness`, restricted to the active
build configuration. It MUST compare exact counts rather than rounded displayed
percentages, average file percentages, or impose an 80% target within each
function. A file whose executable code is not measured MUST require exception
evidence rather than pass with a fabricated percentage. A file established to
contain no executable coverage obligations MUST be reported as such and MUST
NOT require a threshold exception.
Absence of recorded instrumented lines alone MUST NOT establish that a file
contains no executable coverage obligations.
:::{req} check.functions
Every function under {cite}`requirements.test-coverage.check.scope` without
recorded execution attributable to it MUST have current accepted exception
evidence under {cite}`requirements.test-coverage.check.exceptions`, even when
its containing file meets the target of
{cite}`requirements.test-coverage.check.threshold`.
Execution attributable only to another function, including a nested function
or closure, MUST NOT establish coverage of the enclosing function merely
because their source locations overlap. Having no recorded lines alone MUST
NOT establish that a function has no executable coverage obligations.
:::{req} check.exceptions
An unmet file threshold or an unexecuted or not-measured function MAY satisfy
the coverage policy only
through current, accepted, independently assessed evidence explaining why its
coverage is incomplete. An exception MUST be attached to the source file or
function whose incomplete coverage it justifies. A file-threshold exception
MUST NOT automatically excuse untested functions.
An exception MUST NOT excuse another source item's incomplete coverage.
Changes to the source item, justification, or other inputs
of its citation review MUST invalidate the affected exception under
{cite}`requirements.references.citation_review`.
A source comment or unassessed justification alone MUST NOT count as accepted
exception evidence. Function and gap identities MUST remain portable between
equivalent local and CI checkouts rather than depend on checkout paths,
run identifiers, timestamps, or process identifiers.
